def: The PCIe packet that carries a request, completion or message between two Transaction Layers: a 3- or 4-DW header, an optional data payload and an optional ECRC digest.
DW0 bits [31:29] of a non-Flit TLP header: says whether the header is 3 or 4 DW and whether a data payload follows (100b marks a TLP prefix).
DW0 bits [28:24] of a non-Flit TLP header; with Fmt it identifies the TLP kind (memory, I/O, configuration, message with routing, completion, AtomicOp).
A PCIe request that receives no completion: Memory Write and Messages. The sender is done once the TLP is transmitted.
A PCIe request that must be answered by one or more completions: Memory Read, I/O Read/Write, Configuration Read/Write, AtomicOps (and Deferrable Memory Write in recent revisions).
The TLP that answers a non-posted request, routed by Requester ID and matched by Transaction ID. CplD carries data; Cpl carries none and is also used for error statuses (UR, CA, CRS).
Requester ID plus Tag: the identifier that must be unique among a requester's outstanding non-posted requests and that matches completions to requests.
The Bus/Device/Function number of the function that issued a request (Bus and an 8-bit Function with ARI); completions are routed back to it and IOMMUs use it to select a translation context.
The Bus/Device/Function of the function that generated a completion, in completion header DW1 [31:16].
The requester-chosen number in a request header that distinguishes its outstanding non-posted requests; 5 bits by default, 8 with Extended Tags, 10 with 10-bit tags, 14 in Flit Mode.

The requester-side mechanism that declares a non-posted request failed if its completions do not arrive within the range set in Device Control 2 (default 50 µs to 50 ms); reported as an uncorrectable AER error.
In PCIe 6.x Flit Mode, optional header DWs appended to a base TLP header to carry fields that only some TLPs need.
The usage model PCIe ordering is designed around: a producer writes data then a flag; a consumer that sees the flag must then see the data.
Completion header field (12 bits): bytes remaining to complete the read request, including the bytes in this completion; 0 means 4096.
Completion header field (7 bits): low address bits of the first byte of data in this completion; used with Byte Count to place split completions.
Completion header bit set only by PCI-X completers; PCIe completers must not set it.
TLP attribute that permits the TLP carrying it to pass earlier posted requests; may be set only when Enable Relaxed Ordering is set in Device Control.
TLP attribute saying hardware cache snooping is not required for the access; a coherency hint, not an ordering rule.
TLP attribute that limits ordering to TLPs from the same source ID, letting traffic from different requesters pass each other.
3-bit header field mapping a TLP to a Virtual Channel; ordering rules apply only within the same TC.
Optional 1-DW TLP digest, present when TD = 1, checked by the final receiver; complements the per-link LCRC.
A TLP whose EP bit is set, marking its payload as known bad; the receiver reports Poisoned TLP Received.
4-bit fields in request headers enabling individual bytes of the first and last DW of a request.
Device Control enable that lets a function use all 8 bits of the Tag field (256 outstanding requests) instead of the 5-bit default.
PCIe 4.0+ capability extending the Tag to 10 bits using header bits T9/T8; usable only when requester, completer and path support it.
A mechanism letting a device use unused Function Number bits as extra Tag bits.
AER error reported by a requester that receives a completion matching none of its outstanding requests.
Non-posted PCIe request (FetchAdd, Swap, CAS) executed as a read-modify-write at the completer, which returns the original value in a CplD.
A memory read with Length 1 and both byte enables 0000b; used to flush earlier posted writes.
PCIe 6.0+ link mode carrying TLPs in fixed-size FEC-protected flits, with a different TLP header encoding.
